clue.text: Male model to talk about mirror

indicators.note: a mirror shows things back to front, so the result is read from right to left
about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A male model is told to talk to his own reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside GAS to make GATS, which read backwards is STAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and the word is also used for men alone, as in a stag party.

clue.text: Schedule tax on electronic till

parts.note: a rota is a timetable of duties
value added tax
E is the usual abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail; on joins it

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is told to schedule tax on the electronic cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electronic till' looks like a cash register; till is really the verb meaning to work the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotavate is to break up soil with a rotary cultivator, which is one way to till the ground.

clue.text: Conduct metal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to guide or direct
second meaning: the heavy grey element Pb

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead people is to guide them, and lead is also a soft heavy element used in pipes and roofing.

clue.text: Was Keir wrong to steal Tory leader's sports equipment?

indicators.note: to steal something is to take it in and hold it, so one piece ends up inside the other
if the letters are wrong they need to be put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A political jibe asks whether Keir Starmer stole a Conservative leader's water-sports kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Water-skis are the long boards a skier stands on while towed behind a boat, so they count as sports equipment.

clue.text: Most unhappy footballer drilled by head of Leeds United

indicators.note: something drilled has a hole bored into it, so other letters sit inside it

parts.note: George Best, the Manchester United and Northern Ireland star

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Leeds
U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A footballer is miserable after a drilling from the Leeds United manager.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue means sad or low in spirits, so the superlative bluest means saddest of all.

clue.text: Bride's excited by ring during dance with attractive young lady

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the jumbled letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: an excited thing is stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging; the 's is joined to excited, as in 'is excited'
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A bride, thrilled by her ring, dances at her wedding with a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on Bride's stands for 'is', so the bride is what is excited; the dance is the outer word, not the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Barbie doll is used informally, often dismissively, for a conventionally pretty but vapid young woman, after the toy.

clue.text: Perhaps Ahab's wife is more healthy

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
hale means healthy, so haler is healthier

explanation.surface: It sounds like gossip that Ahab's wife is in better health than he is.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Ahab hunts the white whale in Moby-Dick; 'perhaps' signals he is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahab commands the whaling ship Pequod, so he is an example of a whaler, a person who hunts whales.

clue.text: Photograph of gunners surrounded by axes

indicators.note: something surrounded by others is enclosed on both sides, so it sits between them

parts.note: x and y are the two axes of a graph
the Royal Artillery are the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: A picture shows artillerymen ringed by men with axes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' suggests chopping tools; it is the plural of axis, the x and y lines of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-ray is a radiograph, an image of the inside of the body made with radiation, so a kind of photograph.

clue.text: Cut disease with unlimited money

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis

indicators.note: without limits means without its boundaries, so the outermost letters go and the middle stays

parts.note: the middle letters of money

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a disease off using unlimited funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A T-bone is a steak cut from the loin containing a T-shaped bone, so a cut of meat.

clue.text: Odin's hall after being renovated

indicators.note: something being renovated is rebuilt, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Odin's great hall, Valhalla, is newly done up.
explanation.definitionFit: All-father is a title of Odin in Norse mythology, as the chief god and father of gods and men.

clue.text: Jump from £1,000 plane close to France

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of France

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker leaps from a pricey jet landing near France.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand jeté is a ballet leap from one foot to the other with legs split, a big jump.

clue.text: British Jack leaves pudding in stomach

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer present, so that letter drops out

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
J is jack in a card pack
jelly is a wobbly dessert

explanation.surface: A British sailor walks away with a pudding in his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jack is a British sailor in the surface; here it is the card abbreviation J, taken out of JELLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Belly is an everyday synonym for the stomach or abdomen.

clue.text: Church has real trouble with saint 29

definitions.note: a cross-reference to 29 down: the answer is a king's name, not a word meaning king

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A church is in real difficulty over a royal saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 down is KING, so the definition is a king; Charles is the name of several British monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles I, II and III have all reigned in Britain, so Charles is the name of a king.

clue.text: Ministerial material?

parts.note: surface reading: papers or briefings that a government minister uses; setter's reading: the fabric a church minister wears, whose name also stands for the clergy as a body

explanation.walkthrough: Minister means a member of the clergy, not a government official; the clergy are collectively known as 'the cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is an idiom for the clergy, from their distinctive dress, and it is literally a fabric.

clue.text: Creature can feel it's evolving

indicators.note: something evolving changes form over time, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An animal senses that it is changing under natural selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf insect is a tropical insect camouflaged to look like a leaf, so it is a living creature.

clue.text: Proposition me with other design

indicators.note: a design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are laid out anew

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone is propositioned along with a third party, by design.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition proved from axioms, and proposition is the formal term for such a statement.

clue.text: Setter's covering three quarks in a neutron — confused?

indicators.note: a covering goes round the outside of something, so these letters enclose the rest

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: my
a neutron is made of one up and two down quarks, abbreviated u, d, d

explanation.surface: A physics puzzle about the quark content of a neutron leaves the reader baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddy thinking is unclear, so muddy can mean muddled or confused.

clue.text: Ball game's chaotic conclusion

parts.note: a ball is round like the letter O

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A ball game ends in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, so it stands for the end or conclusion.

clue.text: (√-1 + 50) ÷ 50? That's difficult

parts.note: the square root of minus one is i in mathematics, and 50 is L in Roman numerals
division writes one thing over another, so another Roman 50 goes after it

explanation.surface: A sum mixing imaginary and Roman numbers is admitted to be hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the sum as letters: I plus L, then a further L.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can mean hard or difficult, as in 'ill at ease' or 'it ill becomes him'.

clue.text: Portrait to hang over 29's head

indicators.note: over here means covering on all sides, so one piece encloses the next

parts.note: the way a garment hangs is the way it lies
29 down is king, abbreviated K in chess
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A portrait is to be hung above a royal's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the top of the king; it is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness, and 29 down is KING, shortened to K.
explanation.definitionFit: A likeness is a picture or representation of someone, which is what a portrait is.

clue.text: Decided to put page in dictionary? About time

indicators.note: putting something in a thing places it inside
about means going round, so the big word wraps another letter

parts.note: the Oxford English Dictionary
p is short for page
t is short for time

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to add a page to the dictionary, and about time too.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opted is a synonym of decided in the past tense.

clue.text: Wonder that not even Juliet married a prince

indicators.note: keeping what is not even means keeping only the odd-numbered letters

parts.note: the first and third letters of that
Juliet is J in the phonetic alphabet
m is short for married
taken as written
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: It is a wonder that not even Juliet married a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the marble mausoleum at Agra.

clue.text: Who's moved by Heather crying?

indicators.note: something moved is shifted out of place, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
ling is common heather

explanation.surface: Someone asks which person was so touched by a woman named Heather that they wept.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Howling is crying loudly, whether in grief or like a baby, so the two words overlap.

clue.text: Former F1 commentator, one not going by car?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Murray ..., the BBC's long-serving Formula One voice
second meaning: a person who travels on foot

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the most famous motor-racing commentator has a name meaning a pedestrian.
explanation.definitionFit: Murray Walker commentated on Formula One for decades, and a walker is someone who goes on foot rather than driving.

clue.text: Large cup for a small mouth?

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
-let is a suffix meaning a small one, as in piglet

explanation.surface: It asks, playfully, why a big cup would suit a little mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the word for a large cup looks like a small gob.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking vessel with a stem and foot, typically larger than an ordinary cup.

clue.text: Woman completes 29 + 18, the spoilsport

parts.note: 29 down is king, abbreviated K
the answer to 18 across
Joy is a woman's name, and she comes last to complete the word

explanation.surface: A woman finishes a sum and is called a spoilsport for it.
explanation.walkthrough: K plus ILL is completed by JOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is a person who spoils others' fun, which is exactly what a spoilsport does.

clue.text: Quickly eats starter of fish during unhurried retreat

indicators.note: a retreat is a movement backwards, so the letters are read from the end
during means in the middle of, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: unhurried means slow

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of fish

explanation.surface: A diner gulps down the fish course during a leisurely withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: F goes into SLOW after the S, and the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is to eat it greedily and fast, so wolfs means quickly eats.

clue.text: Cried over exercise, putting on weight

indicators.note: putting on clothes means wrapping them around oneself, so the outer letters wear the inner ones

parts.note: wt is the abbreviation for weight

indicators.note: over can mean turned over, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Someone sobbed about their workout because they had gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting on weight' reads as gaining pounds; here the weight abbreviation puts the turned-round exercise on like a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wept is the past tense of weep, meaning shed tears, so it matches cried.

clue.text: Standard book on furniture

indicators.note: in an across entry one piece sitting on another follows it, so the book goes second

parts.note: a bench is a long seat
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A standard book is placed on a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, X on Y puts X after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A benchmark is a standard or point of reference against which things are measured.

clue.text: Son goes to the basement in closed buildings

indicators.text: Son goes to the basement in
indicators.note: in a down entry the basement is the bottom, so the son's letter moves from top to foot of the word

parts.note: shut means closed

explanation.surface: A son retreats downstairs inside shuttered buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: S for son moves from the top of SHUT to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Huts are small simple buildings or shelters.

clue.text: Royal family's supported by government

indicators.note: in a down entry being supported means sitting above, so the second piece comes underneath

parts.note: kin are relatives
g is short for government

explanation.surface: The royal family relies on the government's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male monarch, so a royal, the noun for a member of the reigning family.

clue.text: Child's hero in Paris on vacation with clergy

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
vacated means emptied, so the inside goes and only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of Paris
Jack Reacher is the hero of Lee Child's thrillers

explanation.surface: A child's idol is holidaying in Paris with some priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like a youngster; it is the author Lee Child, whose hero is Jack Reacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachers are ministers who deliver sermons, so collectively they are clergy.

clue.text: Ashley Olsen, say, bored by American writer

indicators.note: something bored by another has it drilled into it, so a letter goes inside

parts.note: Ashley Olsen has a twin sister, Mary-Kate; 'say' marks her as an example
A is short for American

explanation.surface: An actress is found tedious by a US author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' suggests tedium; here it means drilled into. Mark Twain is the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, author of Huckleberry Finn, is a famous American writer.
